data.title: Anogenital warts — viva
data.summary: Sexually transmitted infections · 12 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Anogenital warts** (Sexually transmitted infections)_

**Q1. What are anogenital warts? Which HPV types?**
- Commonest viral STI — benign epithelial proliferations of anogenital skin and mucosa
- ~90% due to low-risk HPV 6 and 11; co-infection with high-risk types (16, 18, 31, 33) possible
- Incubation 3 weeks to 8 months (average 2–3 months); many infections subclinical

**Q2. Describe the clinical types.**
- Condyloma acuminata: soft, pink, filiform/cauliflower-like papillomas on moist areas (prepuce, frenulum, coronal sulcus, vulva, introitus, perianal)
- Papular (dome-shaped, keratinised — shaft, pubis), flat/macular (cervix — seen with acetic acid), keratotic (dry skin)
- Giant condyloma (Buschke–Löwenstein tumour)
- Intra-meatal, vaginal, cervical, anal canal (anoscopy in receptive anal sex)

**Q3. What is the acetowhite test?**
- 5% acetic acid for 3–5 min turns HPV-infected epithelium white — helps find subclinical lesions; not specific (any inflamed/traumatised skin)

**Q4. Differential diagnosis.**
- Normal variants: pearly penile papules (rows on corona), vestibular papillae (symmetrical, separate bases), Fordyce spots, sebaceous hyperplasia
- Condyloma lata (secondary syphilis — flat, moist, grey; VDRL positive), molluscum, seborrhoeic keratosis, skin tags, lichen planus, bowenoid papulosis, verrucous carcinoma/SCC, Buschke–Löwenstein tumour

**Q5. When do you biopsy?**
- Atypical (pigmented, indurated, fixed, ulcerated) lesions, immunocompromised patient, no response or worsening on therapy, older patient

**Q6. Discuss treatment options.**
- Patient-applied: podophyllotoxin 0.5% solution/0.15% cream twice daily 3 days per week, up to 4 weeks; imiquimod 5% cream 3 times/week overnight up to 16 weeks; sinecatechins 15% (green-tea extract)
- Provider-applied/ablative: cryotherapy (liquid nitrogen) weekly; TCA 80–90%; podophyllin 10–25% in tincture benzoin (wash off after 1–4 h; max 0.5 ml/10 cm² per session); electrocautery, radiofrequency, CO2 laser, scissor excision
- Choice depends on number, size, site, keratinisation, cost, pregnancy

**Q7. Write a short note on podophyllin (PYQ).**
- Resin from Podophyllum emodi (Indian) or P. peltatum; active podophyllotoxin binds tubulin → arrests mitosis in metaphase → necrosis of wart
- Podophyllin is non-standardised and contains mutagenic flavonoids; podophyllotoxin is purified and safer for self-use
- Toxicity: local erosion; systemic absorption from large areas/mucosa → peripheral neuropathy, myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity, coma
- Contraindicated in pregnancy, on cervix/urethra/anal canal, bleeding lesions

**Q8. Management in pregnancy.**
- Warts enlarge and become friable; avoid podophyllin, podophyllotoxin, (imiquimod — limited data)
- Cryotherapy, TCA, excision/electrocautery
- Caesarean only if warts obstruct the birth canal or would bleed heavily; risk of juvenile recurrent respiratory papillomatosis in baby is low

**Q9. What about warts in children?**
- Consider sexual abuse but also vertical transmission (up to 2–3 years), autoinoculation from hand warts, non-sexual household spread; careful history and examination, involve paediatric team

**Q10. What other evaluation and counselling is needed?**
- Screen for other STIs (HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B), examine partner, Pap smear/HPV test for women (cervical screening), anoscopy if anal warts
- Explain recurrence (~30% within 3 months), condoms reduce but don't eliminate transmission, HPV vaccination

**Q11. Discuss cervical intraepithelial neoplasia link (PYQ).**
- High-risk HPV (16, 18) E6 binds p53, E7 binds Rb → cell-cycle dysregulation → CIN 1–3 → invasive cancer
- Screening: Pap smear (cytology), HPV DNA test, VIA/VILI (visual inspection in low-resource settings)
- Prevention: HPV vaccine before sexual debut

**Q12. What is the role of HPV vaccines in genital warts?**
- Quadrivalent and nonavalent vaccines (contain 6, 11) prevent ~90% of genital warts — reduction seen in vaccinated populations (Australia); not therapeutic for existing warts

## Quick spotter facts
- Acetowhitening — subclinical HPV
- HPV 6/11 — 90% of genital warts
- Pearly penile papules are normal — don't treat

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (HPV, genital warts); NACO National Technical Guidelines on RTI/STI (syndromic management, colour-coded kits). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
